title: Flash Flood Warning
description: FFWPHI The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a * Flash Flood Warning for... Northwestern Burlington County in southern New Jersey... Southeastern Bucks County in southeastern Pennsylvania... East Central Montgomery County in southeastern Pennsylvania... Northeastern Philadelphia County in southeastern Pennsylvania... * Until 730 PM EST. * At 327 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain across portions of the warned area. Up to a 0.5 inch of rain has fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1.5 to 2.5 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is expected to begin shortly. HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms. SOURCE...Radar indicated. IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor drainage and low-lying areas. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Philadelphia, Bensalem, Mount Laurel, Willingboro, Florence, Burlington, Bristol, Mount Holly, Riverside, Hatboro, Beverly and Yardley.

title: Flood Advisory
description: ...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas... Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County. .The river gauge at Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias continues to fall steadily this afternoon, and is now expected to drop below action stage early Friday morning. The latest forecast has gauge levels falling well below bankfull over the weekend, and remaining so into early next week. For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river levels are forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues along the creek banks. * WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias. * WHEN...Until Friday morning. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 12:15 PM CST Thursday the stage was 6.85 feet and falling. - Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet. - The level has fallen from 8.7 feet at 5 PM Wednesday to below 7 feet just before noon Thursday. - Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 2.1 feet early Tuesday afternoon, November 17th. - Action stage is 5.0 feet. - Flood stage is 11.0 feet. - https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues. * WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona... Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 1140 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with flow peaking at 3000 cfs. - Flooding is expected along the Gila River. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Advisory
description: * WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides. * WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait, and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County. * WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots, roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 937 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding. - The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local time): * Port Chicago: 1.2 ft above normal (6.1 ft MLLW) at 2:15 PM Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 2:56 PM Fri 11/13, 0.7 ft above normal (5.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/14, and 0.3 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 4:39 PM Sun 11/15. * West Sacramento: 1.2 ft above normal (5.5 ft MLLW) at 5:28 PM Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.4 ft MLLW) at 6:10 PM Fri 11/13, 0.9 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 6:57 PM Sat 11/14, and 0.6 ft above normal (5.0 ft MLLW) at 7:50 PM Sun 11/15. * Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Thu 11/12, +7.7 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/13, and +7.6 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/14. - These predictions include up to +1.1 feet of storm surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. Timing of high tide may vary up to an hour throughout the San Francisco Bay and Delta. - Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at: * Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre dictions.html?id=9415144 * West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide predictions.html?id=9416131 * Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a Flood Warning for the following rivers in Texas... Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County. For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast. Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp. * WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden. * WHEN...From Sunday afternoon until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below Cotulla to below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill. Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 AM CST Thursday the stage was 8.5 feet. - Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early Sunday afternoon and continue rising to a crest of 15.0 feet Monday morning. - Flood stage is 14.0 feet. - Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.2 feet on 09/19/1983. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Special Marine Warning
description: SMWBOX The National Weather Service in Boston/Norton has issued a * Special Marine Warning for... Coastal Waters extending out to 25 NM South of Marthas Vineyard and Nantucket... Coastal waters from Provincetown MA to Chatham MA to Nantucket MA out 20 NM... Ocean Waters from Marthas Vineyard to Nantucket from 25 to 60 NM... Ocean Waters from Provincetown to Nantucket from 20 to 60 NM... * Until 815 PM EST. * At 710 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing waterspouts was located 36 nm southeast of The Coastal Waters South Of Nantucket, moving northeast at 25 knots. HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater. SOURCE...Radar. IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and suddenly higher waves. * The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
